> Original MUI X documentation: [Simple Tree View - Selection](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/selection/). The examples of this page are written for R.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(muiTreeView)
library(htmltools)

# Some functions of muiMaterial, muiCharts and reactRouter, used in all the examples of this page
pkg_items <- function() {
  list(
    TreeItem(
      itemId = "muiMaterial",
      label = "muiMaterial",
      TreeItem(itemId = "muiMaterial::Button", label = "Button()"),
      TreeItem(itemId = "muiMaterial::TextField", label = "TextField()"),
      TreeItem(itemId = "muiMaterial::Drawer", label = "Drawer()")
    ),
    TreeItem(
      itemId = "muiCharts",
      label = "muiCharts",
      TreeItem(itemId = "muiCharts::BarChart", label = "BarChart()"),
      TreeItem(itemId = "muiCharts::LineChart", label = "LineChart()")
    ),
    TreeItem(
      itemId = "reactRouter",
      label = "reactRouter",
      TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter::RouterProvider", label = "RouterProvider()"),
      TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter::Route", label = "Route()"),
      TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter::NavLink", label = "NavLink()")
    )
  )
}
```

## Single selection

By default, one item can be selected at a time: click on an item, or focus it and press <kbd>Space</kbd>. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/selection/#single-selection)

```{r}
SimpleTreeView(pkg_items())
```

## Multi-selection

Use `multiSelect = TRUE` to select several items: hold <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> (<kbd>⌘ Command</kbd> on macOS) while clicking, or <kbd>Shift</kbd> to select a range. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/selection/#multi-selection)

```{r}
SimpleTreeView(multiSelect = TRUE, pkg_items())
```

## Disable selection

Use `disableSelection = TRUE` to prevent the selection of all items. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/selection/#disable-selection)

```{r}
SimpleTreeView(disableSelection = TRUE, pkg_items())
```

## Checkbox selection

Use `checkboxSelection = TRUE` to render a checkbox next to each item. Combine it with `multiSelect = TRUE` to check several items. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/selection/#checkbox-selection)

```{r}
SimpleTreeView(checkboxSelection = TRUE, pkg_items())
```

```{r}
SimpleTreeView(checkboxSelection = TRUE, multiSelect = TRUE, pkg_items())
```

## Selectable items

Use `disableSelection = TRUE` on a `TreeItem()` to make only this item unselectable. Here, only the functions can be selected, not their packages. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/selection/#selectable-items)

```{r}
SimpleTreeView(
  checkboxSelection = TRUE,
  multiSelect = TRUE,
  defaultExpandedItems = list("muiCharts", "reactRouter"),
  TreeItem(
    itemId = "muiCharts",
    label = "muiCharts",
    disableSelection = TRUE,
    TreeItem(itemId = "muiCharts::BarChart", label = "BarChart()"),
    TreeItem(itemId = "muiCharts::LineChart", label = "LineChart()")
  ),
  TreeItem(
    itemId = "reactRouter",
    label = "reactRouter",
    disableSelection = TRUE,
    TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter::RouterProvider", label = "RouterProvider()"),
    TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter::Route", label = "Route()"),
    TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter::NavLink", label = "NavLink()")
  )
)
```

## Default selection

Use `defaultSelectedItems` to select items when the tree is created. With `multiSelect = TRUE`, give the ids in a `list()`. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/selection/#controlled-selection)

```{r}
SimpleTreeView(
  multiSelect = TRUE,
  checkboxSelection = TRUE,
  defaultExpandedItems = list("muiCharts"),
  defaultSelectedItems = list("muiCharts::BarChart", "muiCharts::LineChart"),
  pkg_items()
)
```

## Controlled selection

Use `selectedItems` with `onSelectedItemsChange` to control the selection from your app, for example from the Shiny server with `renderReact()`. See [controlled state in Shiny](shiny.html#controlled-state-from-the-server). [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/selection/#controlled-selection)

`onSelectedItemsChange` receives the ids of all the selected items. In Shiny, use `onSelectedItemsChange = setInput("selected", 1)` to get them in `input$selected`. On this page, a `JS()` function writes them below the tree:

```{r}
div(
  SimpleTreeView(
    multiSelect = TRUE,
    checkboxSelection = TRUE,
    onSelectedItemsChange = JS(
      "(event, itemIds) => { document.getElementById('stv-selected').textContent = JSON.stringify(itemIds); }"
    ),
    pkg_items()
  ),
  tags$pre("Selected items: ", tags$span(id = "stv-selected", "[]"))
)
```

## Track item selection change

Use `onItemSelectionToggle` to know which item was just selected or deselected. It receives the event, the item id and whether the item is now selected. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/selection/#track-item-selection-change)

```{r}
div(
  SimpleTreeView(
    multiSelect = TRUE,
    checkboxSelection = TRUE,
    onItemSelectionToggle = JS(
      "(event, itemId, isSelected) => {
        document.getElementById('stv-toggle').textContent =
          itemId + (isSelected ? ' was selected' : ' was deselected');
      }"
    ),
    pkg_items()
  ),
  tags$pre(tags$span(id = "stv-toggle", "No item selection recorded"))
)
```

## Automatic parents and children selection

With `multiSelect = TRUE`, use `selectionPropagation` to select the children of a selected parent (`descendants = TRUE`), and the parent when all its children are selected (`parents = TRUE`). Only the expanded items are considered by `SimpleTreeView()`. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/rich-tree-view/selection/#automatic-parents-and-children-selection)

```{r}
SimpleTreeView(
  multiSelect = TRUE,
  checkboxSelection = TRUE,
  defaultExpandedItems = list("muiMaterial", "muiCharts"),
  selectionPropagation = list(descendants = TRUE, parents = TRUE),
  pkg_items()
)
```

## Imperative API

The MUI imperative API (`apiRef`, to select an item or read its selection status from JavaScript) relies on a React hook, which is not available from R. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/selection/#imperative-api)

## API

- [`TreeItem()`](../reference/TreeItem.html) – [MUI API](https://mui.com/x/api/tree-view/tree-item/)
